questions.question: How do layouts and partials fit into Rails MVC views?
questions.title: Layouts and Partials in MVC Views
questions.direct_answer: In the view layer, layouts and partials organize HTML. A layout (application.html.erb) is the shell that wraps every action: <head>, nav, and <%= yield %> where the action's view renders. A partial (_form.html.erb) is a reusable snippet rendered with render 'form'. MVC-wise: the controller renders the action's view, that view renders inside the layout, and both can render partials. So a page is composed: layout wraps the view, the view reuses partials. This keeps HTML DRY — the nav lives in the layout, a shared form in a partial, and the action's unique content in its view. Use partials for repeated UI (cards, forms) and layouts for the page frame.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know a layout wraps the action view (yield) and a partial is a reusable snippet (render 'name'), composing a page DRY.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Forgetting yield in the layout (no action content), or naming a partial without the underscore.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Layout = shell wrapping the action (yield); partial = reusable snippet (render 'name'). A page composes layout -> view -> partials. Keeps HTML DRY.
